title: Natural cochain counit of completed-coefficient reduction
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l and any scheme W, with independent site and coefficient universes. Let S be a coherent derived reduction calculus [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] and let M be an ordinary quotient-tensor/limit model [def-trf-completion-unit-models]. There is a natural transformation epsilon from Q followed by S.reduction to M.quotient followed by Q, on all cochain complexes over the completed E-coefficient sheaf. For every flat-term K-flat complex P and every finite level n, evaluating epsilon and composing the exact-localization comparison and the termwise M.evaluation n gives S.reductionEvaluation n followed by coefficientFiniteReductionModel. No coefficient extension E to L or direct L-system is involved.

source.place: sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-adjoint (07A6) and lemma-derived-pushforward-composition (0D6E); derived.tex, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors (09T5); step 1 of stage3-pur-extension-strict-derived-comparison.

proof.text: Construct the natural isomorphism between the degreewise ordinary limit and roosLimitFunctor from their limit cones. Transport the standard rightDerivedFunctorUnit of lim through this isomorphism and the quotient-to-homotopy localization factors. The definition of rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso gives its required normalization on K-injective towers. All helpers are constructed and proved privately in the item module.

Whisker the normalized limit unit by coefficient restriction and compose with M.limitComparison and the inverse exact-restriction localization factor. Compose the localization of the ordinary tensor-adjunction unit with this system unit at M.quotient. Apply the inverse of S.adjunction.homEquiv at every complex. Naturality in both variables of homEquiv proves naturality of this transformation; applying homEquiv recovers the prescribed ordinary-unit composite by Equiv.apply_symm_apply.

Apply finiteComparison_of_unit to the constructed natural transformation and the proved ordinary-unit transpose identity. At each good complex P use P.property.1 for K-flatness and P.property.2 for termwise flatness. This gives exactly the stated finite evaluation identity for every n, without extra invertibility or coherence hypotheses.

proof_origin.place: lemma-adjoint (07A6), lemma-derived-pushforward-composition (0D6E), and the existing finiteComparison_of_unit normalization (lem-trf-completion-unit-finite-mate-comparison). Direct adjunction transpose of the localized ordinary unit; standard rightDerivedFunctorUnit supplies the limit comparison.

lean.statement:
theorem coefficientReductionNaturalCochainComparison
    (S : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E W)
    (M : CompletionUnit.OrdinaryModel l E W) :
    ∃ ε : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ S.reduction ⟶
        M.quotient l E W ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q,
      ∀ (P : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E W).FullSubcategory) (n : ℕ),
        (coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E W n).map (ε.app P.obj) ≫
            (coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E W n).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app
              ((M.quotient l E W).obj P.obj) ≫
            DerivedCategory.Q.map
              ((NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex (M.evaluation n) (.up ℤ)).hom.app P.obj) =
          (S.reductionEvaluation n).hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj) ≫
            (coefficientFiniteReductionModel l E W P.obj P.property.1 n).hom
